bindings.title: What is on which light
bindings.intro: A binding is one printer, one light, and one segment of it. A change here applies at once, in the running module.
bindings.segment_rule: A segment carries one printer. Two bindings cannot share one, so a segment already in use is offered greyed out with the printer that has it. One printer may sit on several lights — that is what multi-room status is — at the cost of a second steady stream.
bindings.not_saved: Every change here is written into the module's own configuration store, so it survives a restart and an upgrade. A module purge or a fresh install loses it, so keep a copy of a list you want to keep.
bindings.dialog_intro: The segment list is the light's own — read from the controller as you open this — so a segment the light does not have cannot be chosen. A brightness is only written when the whole light is taken, because the rest of a borrowed strip belongs to its owner.
bindings.brightness_note: written once at start, 0 to 255; empty means the module's own default of 128
bindings.brightness_borrowed: none — a borrowed zone never gets a brightness
bindings.segments_from_light: read from the light itself, never typed
bindings.segments_unreadable: The segments of this light could not be read, so there is nothing to pick from: {why}
bindings.segments_unread_line: its segments could not be read: {why}
bindings.printer_gone: A printer the host no longer holds
bindings.printer_missing: this printer is no longer in Prusa Connect
bindings.zone_handed_back: paused — its zone handed back to its owner
bindings.light_off: paused — the light is switched off
bindings.saved: Saved — the module is running on the new set.
bindings.removed: Removed — that segment is free again.
bindings.load_failed: The bindings could not be read
bindings.lights_failed: The lights could not be read
bindings.empty_body: Add a binding and the light appears here, with the segments it reports of itself.

bindings.discovered_note: This list is empty because nothing in this build sweeps your network for lights. A light becomes known to this module when a binding names its address, so a light it has never been told about cannot appear here.
bindings.discovered_how: The way to add one today is the panel above: name the light's address as a new one, and it appears as its own card with the segments it reports.

bindings.no_test: There is no test per binding. The module's preview routes paint a whole light with a diagnostic picture, so a test belongs on a light rather than on one printer's row, and it arrives with the Devices screen.
events.title: What each moment shows
events.intro: A moment is a transition — a print finishing, a pause, an error — shown for a length and then given back. One light at a time, because the list of moments belongs to the light.
events.load_failed: The moments could not be read
events.no_lights: No light is bound yet, so there is no moment table to show. Put a printer on a light in Bindings, and the light appears here with all eight of its moments.
events.presets_are_theirs: Each moment carries its own setting per printer. Presets are the light’s own — build and tune them in WLED’s own interface, because this page only names one.
events.strip_no_word: This light is a strip: a word needs a second dimension, so it is not offered here, and a moment set to a word shows the moment’s colour instead.
events.shape_unknown: The module has not drawn a frame for this light yet, so it does not know whether it is a panel or a strip. A word is offered; a strip would show the moment’s colour instead.
events.not_kept: This module has no store to keep a change in: {why}
events.each_moment_then_printers: each moment, then a line per printer
events.preset_placeholder: the preset’s name, as WLED spells it
events.word_undrawable: not drawable by this font: {chars} — the module refuses the word and shows the moment’s colour instead
events.word_too_wide: {word} is too wide for a 256 × 64 panel at the module’s scale of five, so the moment’s colour is shown instead
events.reset_done: Reset — that moment is back to its default for that printer.
events.was_default: That moment was already at its default.
events.footnote: A preset takes the whole light for its moment — capture it, run the preset for the length, put it back — and it is refused on a borrowed zone. While a preset runs the progress bar is gone, and that is the trade.
events.for_forever: forever means until its state changes: until it resumes, until it is cleared, until the light answers. A length such as 60s or 5m is accepted too.
events.preset_not_checked: A preset name is stored as written and never checked against the light, because a write that failed while a lamp was off would be the worse defect. No route in this build lists a light’s presets, so the name is typed rather than picked.
events.kept_without_light: A change here is written into the module’s own store, so it survives a restart and an upgrade, and it is kept whether or not the light is answering. Nothing here is sent to the light.
events.unknown_moments: The store holds rows about moments this build does not have, and they are reported rather than deleted: {list}
colours.title: What each state looks like
colours.intro: One row per condition a printer can be in. A state is not a moment: it lasts until something else happens.
colours.note: Every state can carry a word, and the word is yours to edit — which is also how a light is made to speak another language. A word beats the layout while it holds: a light showing a state with a word shows that word, not the bar and digits. It holds forever by default, or for a length you set.
colours.load_failed: The table could not be read
colours.not_kept: This module has no store to keep a change in: {why}
colours.conditions_note: The light unreachable and the printer lost are not words the host reports: this module computes both from its own reading, because a printer it has lost, and one that has gone quiet beside it, have no state to report — and neither must look like a verdict. They are editable here exactly as a state is.
colours.busy_ready_note: BUSY and READY have no row here. The approved screen gives their two places to the light unreachable and the printer lost, and that is this page. The module still holds both states and still paints them; an override already stored for either keeps working, and this page simply does not edit it.
colours.reset_done: Reset — {state} is back to the colour the table gives it, no word, and a hold of forever.
colours.already_default: There was nothing stored for {state}: it was already at its default.
colours.holds_needs_word: A hold belongs to a word: write one to set a length.
colours.not_drawable: not drawable by this font: {chars} — the panel refuses the word and shows the colour instead
colours.too_wide: {word} does not fit a 256 × 64 panel at the module’s scale of five, so the light shows the colour instead
colours.showing_forever: on the light now, and it holds until the state moves
colours.expired_short: not showing — the hold ran out
colours.expired_why: A light is showing this state and the hold ran out, so nothing shows this word now and nothing will until it is written again. Write it again to bring it back.
colours.later_why: No light is showing this state now. The word runs from the moment a light enters the state.
colours.no_word: This state carries no word: it is drawn as the colour alone.
colours.font_note: The font is the limit, not the text: it holds A–Z, 0–9, a space and . - %, which is 40 glyphs — there is no _ and no /. A character outside that set cannot be drawn, so the module refuses the word and shows the colour; write it in capitals and it draws.
colours.kept_note: A change here is written into the module’s own store, and reaches the light on the painter’s next pass. This page sends nothing to the light.
colours.unknown_states: The store holds rows about states this build does not have, and they are reported rather than deleted: {list}
colours.strip_plain: A strip of 48 pixels filled with {colour}; a strip cannot carry a word
